definitions.explanation: The counter {羽|わ} is used for birds of all kinds and, by traditional convention, for rabbits. {一羽|いちわ} counts one such animal. The reading of {羽|わ} changes depending on the number attached to it (e.g., {三羽|さんば}, {六羽|ろっぱ}).

examples.japanese: ⟦{庭|にわ}→庭：02239_niwa⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{雀|すずめ}→雀：05006_suzume⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{一羽|いちわ}とまって⟦いた→いる：00495_iru⟧。
examples.english: A sparrow was perched in the garden.

examples.japanese: ⟦{空|そら}→空：02216_sora⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{見上|みあ}げる→見上げる：04567_miageru⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧、⟦{鶴|つる}→鶴：04359_tsuru⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{一羽|いちわ}⟦ゆっくり→ゆっくり：00910_yukkuri⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{飛|と}んでいた→飛ぶ：00759_tobu⟧。
examples.english: When I looked up at the sky, a single crane was flying slowly.

notes:
Counter for birds and rabbits. Though rabbits are mammals, they have been traditionally counted with ⟦{羽|わ}→羽：01007_wa⟧ rather than ⟦{匹|ひき}→匹：00939_hiki⟧; one common explanation is that Buddhist monks, forbidden from eating four-legged animals, rationalized eating rabbits by classifying them as birds. In modern usage, ⟦{匹|ひき}→匹：00939_hiki⟧ is also widely accepted for rabbits.

COUNTING PATTERN (sound changes):
- {一羽|いちわ} (1)
- {二羽|にわ} (2)
- {三羽|さんば} / さんわ (3) — both readings used
- {四羽|よんわ} (4)
- {五羽|ごわ} (5)
- {六羽|ろっぱ} (6) — note っ and handakuten
- {七羽|ななわ} (7)
- {八羽|はちわ} / はっぱ (8)
- {九羽|きゅうわ} (9)
- {十羽|じゅっぱ} / じっぱ (10)
- {何羽|なんば} / なんわ: how many birds?

USAGE:
- Used for all birds: ⟦{鶏|にわとり}→鶏：05202_niwatori⟧ (chickens), ⟦{雀|すずめ}→雀：05006_suzume⟧ (sparrows), ⟦{鶴|つる}→鶴：04359_tsuru⟧ (cranes), ⟦{鳩|はと}→鳩：05007_hato⟧ (pigeons), ⟦{鴨|かも}→鴨：17740_kamo⟧ (ducks), etc.
- Also traditionally used for ⟦{兎|うさぎ}→兎：01854_usagi⟧ (rabbits), though ⟦{一匹|いっぴき}→一匹：08930_ippiki⟧ is increasingly common in everyday speech.
- Not used for other flying creatures: bats (⟦{蝙蝠|こうもり}→蝙蝠：04354_koumori⟧) take ⟦{匹|ひき}→匹：00939_hiki⟧, and insects take ⟦{匹|ひき}→匹：00939_hiki⟧.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{一匹|いっぴき}→一匹：08930_ippiki⟧: one (small) animal — general counter for mammals, fish, insects, and now often rabbits.
- {一頭|いっとう}: one (large) animal — used for larger mammals like cattle or horses.
